definition: The length of stage n of the convergent schedule: (1/2)^(n+1), which equals the gap between the start time of stage n+1 and the start time of stage n.
note: Stipulated together with DEF-ZENO-STAGE-TIME; the equality with the gap between stage times is proved, not assumed. A shrinking duration is a mathematical schedule property and supplies no physical mechanism for performing ever-faster stages (SU-REAL).
